claims.text: The investigated material is an additively manufactured dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
High-resolution transmission electron microscopy coupled with EDS mapping can elucidate oxidation mechanisms in this alloy.
HR-TEM coupled with EDS mapping can resolve elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
Oxidation testing at 800–1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere is representative of the alloy's proposed high-temperature applications.
Oxidation produces or modifies local elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitate interfaces acts as a diffusion barrier.
The proposed interfacial diffusion barrier affects oxide-scale formation and growth kinetics.
HR-TEM and EDS mapping will reveal compositional heterogeneities at or near nanoprecipitates.
Compositional heterogeneities near nanoprecipitates will correlate with regions of improved oxidation resistance.
Cast or wrought counterparts have less distinct nanoprecipitate features than the additively manufactured alloy.
HR-TEM and EDS observations are limited to local, near-atomic-scale regions.
Macroscopic oxidation behavior may involve factors that are not captured by local HR-TEM and EDS measurements.
